title: Dev Dock Manager
subtitle: Development Environment Manager
description: The original Django dev-box manager: isolated Docker environments for several users on one machine. The Rust version replaced it, but this one carried the load first.
longDescription: A sophisticated development environment management system built with Django and Docker. This platform provides isolated, containerized development environments for multiple users on the same machine, complete with pre-configured tools and packages for various development workflows.
why: dev-dock puts a desktop in a container, but someone still has to run docker for each person. On a shared machine that someone shouldn't be everyone, since holding the Docker socket is close to holding root on the host. So this dashboard sits in between: log in, click create, get your own desktop.
gains: Lets an admin run a shared Linux box for several people from one Users page: create accounts, make admins, disable someone, reset a password. Kept for setups that want Python or the Django admin. Users see only their own desktops; anyone else's answers 404, as if it never existed.
lessons: Container and image lists once took 8.4 s and 13.5 s because docker-py inspected everything on the host. Now: one list call, then only desktops you may see.
The backend lists only containers whose image is named exactly gui-vnc, so a pulled image needs that tag before the dashboard sees anything.
Desktops created before ownership labels existed have no owner, so only admins can see them.
